q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution
Q2 FY2027 earnings release would typically occur approximately 3 months from today (August 23, 2026), likely in late November 2026. This is asking for the *forward guidance* that will be issued at that earnings call—not the actual Q2 FY2027 results, but what management will guide toward for Q3 FY2027.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

Based on the research provided:
- NVIDIA issued forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 on May 20, 2026 of **$91.0 billion ± 2%** (range: $89.2B - $92.8B)
- Analyst consensus estimate is ~$91.9 billion
- NVIDIA has a track record of exceeding guidance (Q1 FY2027 beat by ~$2B)

The question asks what guidance will be issued *in* the Q2 FY2027 earnings release—meaning the forward guidance for Q3 FY2027. 

Given:
- Q1 FY2027 reported $81.6B (20% sequential growth)
- Q2 FY2027 guided to $91.0B midpoint (12% sequential growth expected, a deceleration from Q1's 20%)
- Historical pattern shows NVIDIA beating guidance by ~$2B
- Analyst expectations tend to be ~1% above midpoint

The most likely forward guidance issued in the Q2 earnings release for Q3 FY2027 would be somewhere in the **$100-105B range**, reflecting continued strong but decelerating sequential growth (10-15% from the ~$91B Q2 expectation).

However, the range provided (99.5B to 115.5B) is quite wide and the research doesn't contain specific forward guidance numbers for quarters beyond Q2 FY2027.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Macro slowdown or recession concerns emerging in Q2 2026
- AI capex spending cycle cooling faster than expected
- China export restrictions tightening further
- Competitive pressures from AMD or other manufacturers intensifying
- Management taking a more conservative stance given potential market saturation concerns
- Guidance could be as low as $95-100B if growth deceleration accelerates

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Stronger-than-expected demand for AI compute and inference workloads in Q2
- Upside surprise in actual Q2 results enabling more aggressive Q3 guidance
- New data center wins or customer commitments announced
- Better-than-expected margins driving revenue upside
- Management maintaining aggressive growth assumptions (15%+ sequential growth)
- Historical pattern of beating guidance suggests midpoint could be 2-3% conservative
- Guidance could reach $105-110B+ if momentum remains strong

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided word-for-word:
- Q1 FY2027: $81.6B reported (20% sequential growth)
- Q2 FY2027: $91.0B midpoint guided (implying ~12% sequential growth)
- Q1 beat guidance by ~$2B
- Analysts estimate Q2 at ~$91.9B (1% above midpoint)

The pattern suggests a deceleration in sequential growth (20% → 12% → presumably ~10-12% for Q3), but with a consistent bias toward beating guided midpoints.

---

## Reasoning on the range provided (99.5B to 115.5B):

The range is quite wide. Given:
- Expected sequential growth from Q2 ($91B) of 10-15% would put Q3 guidance at $100-105B
- Historical beat pattern of ~2% above midpoint
- Continued deceleration in growth rates is typical for maturing mega-cap companies
- Risk of downside if macro conditions deteriorate

The median should be around $102-103B (representing ~12-13% sequential growth from expected Q2 of $91B, with slight upside from historical beating pattern). The 10th percentile (downside scenario) around $98-100B if growth significantly decelerates. The 90th percentile around $108-110B if momentum proves stronger.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, projected $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This guidance implies a range between $89.2 billion and $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is approximately $91.9 billion, placing it within NVIDIA's guided range and about 1% above the midpoint [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This outlook does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/).

For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion, exceeding its own guidance by about $2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This represented an 85% year-over-year increase and 20% sequential growth from the previous quarter [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). Analysts anticipate NVIDIA will continue its trend of slightly exceeding estimates [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
